winner.hypothesis: Replacing the per-byte inString handling in LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L247-251) with a dedicated string-skip inner loop whose body is a 4x-unrolled fast reject (skip while buf[i..i+3] are all > 0x5c), with backslash pairs consumed inline and `escaped` carried across chunk boundaries, will raise the primary speedup from 0.898 to ~1.40-1.59, because ~75% of fixture bytes are string bytes > 0x5c that currently each pay a full outer-loop iteration plus three state checks. This is the only change: the switch cases, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

losers.hypothesis: Adding an outer non-structural skip loop to LineIndex.build (outside strings, once lineHasContent is true, advance i over every byte whose Uint8Array(256) class entry is 0, i.e. anything except '"' '{' '[' '}' ']' '\n', before the switch) removes per-byte switch dispatch for the ~25% of bytes that sit outside strings, with identical output. Single change: only the outside-string path of the existing for-loop gains the skip; the string branch, checkpoint logic, record pushes, for-await loop and all state locals are unchanged.

failure_analysis.what: Median primary 0.869 (runs 0.878, 0.869, 0.675) vs baseline 0.898; correctness 1 in all runs. cur_median_mb_s 496.93 / 481.84 / 374.28 vs ref ~555-569.
failure_analysis.why: The skip loop only touches the ~25% of bytes outside strings, and many of those are structural (" { } [ ] \n) or on content-free line prefixes, so few bytes are actually skipped while every outside-string byte now pays an extra lineHasContent + OCLS table check before the switch. Net effect is neutral-to-slightly-negative, consistent with the plan's own estimate (~0%). Run 3 is likely contaminated by machine contention: its first ~43 ratios cluster at ~0.62-0.70 and then jump to ~0.85-0.93, a bimodal pattern typical of external load rather than the code change. Excluding it, runs 1-2 (0.878, 0.869) are still ~2-3% under baseline, inside the ~4% noise band but on the low side.
failure_analysis.lesson: An outside-string skip alone does not pay for its extra per-byte guard when 75% of bytes are inside strings; it should only be tried stacked with a faster string-scanning loop, where the outer path becomes a larger share of cost. Benchmark runs with bimodal ratio distributions should be treated as contention-affected.

losers.hypothesis: For Array inputs, replacing the `for await (const raw of handle)` chunk iteration in LineIndex.build with a plain index-based `for` loop (inside the same async build, same locals, no extracted function, no state object) removes the per-chunk async-from-sync-iterator wrapping and microtask hop, and that change alone measurably affects the sealed benchmark's speedup. Non-array inputs keep `for await` unchanged. Single change: input iteration shape only.

failure_analysis.what: Replacing `for await` with an index-based `for` loop for Array inputs in LineIndex.build gave primary scores 0.880 / 0.887 / 0.882 (median 0.882) vs baseline 0.898. Correctness stayed 1 in all three runs. cur_median_mb_s was 493.68 / 514.32 / 515.68 against ref 563.00 / 577.03 / 581.51.
failure_analysis.why: The benchmark feeds about 16 chunks per 16 MB build, so the async-from-sync iterator wrapper and microtask hop cost a few microseconds per chunk against a build of roughly 30 ms. The per-byte scan loop dominates, with most bytes inside strings. The -0.016 gap to baseline is smaller than the ~4% run-to-run spread, so this is a null result, not a real slowdown. It matches the plan's own estimate of 0.85-0.95.
failure_analysis.lesson: Chunk iteration shape (for-await vs sync index loop) does not affect this benchmark. Round 1's sync scanChunk kernel (0.897) and the research brief's d1/d2 scratch runs showed the same thing. Future rounds should target per-byte work in the inner scan loop, mainly the in-string fast path, not per-chunk overhead.
